items.title: Junior Mance Part I interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995…
items.q: do you remember Artie Shaw and his Gramercy Five? They made a record with the harpsichord

ctx.x: How is the touch different from a piano?

Oh, man. You just barely touch it. And that threw me too, how it’s played. I was playing it with the same touch as a piano. No you just play it very feathery. Yeah. It’s quite different. And they don’t stay in tune very long. If you play it like you play a piano, you’ve got to tune it after every selection. In fact they had a tuner there that had to tune mine after every take, just to be sure. Yeah you have to play it very lightly. And then after that there were other people that played harpsichord, but they had…
Tell us about the first time you heard bebop. And do you remember what your reaction was?

items.title: Junior Mance Part II interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 18, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I think it was Johnny Guarnieri, with the Gramercy Five Artie Shaw band.

ctx.x: Where did the idea come from to use the harpsichord?

Actually there was a harpsichord in the studio. Somebody must have recorded some harpsichord music maybe before that and I was just fooling around with it, and the producer said, “Hey, let’s do a tune with you playing harpsichord.” I said, “Yeah, why not?” And we did. It’s been done before, I’m not the first one to do that. Johnny Guarnieri did it when he was with — I think it was Johnny Guarnieri, with the Gramercy Five Artie Shaw band. Yeah, they did a bunch of things with a harpsichord and a five piece combo.…
Did you ever have an occasion to use the Rhodes?
